page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical Intel Xeon core operating at 2.3 GHz with hyperthreading enabled. It is configured with 8.0 GB of memory, delivering a balanced ratio of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 45 MB of L3 cache, hardware AES encryption, and AVX support, though newer extensions like AVX-512 and AMX are not available. The instance includes neither bundled local NVMe storage nor GPU acceleration, relying entirely on network-attached storage for disk operations.

Benchmark data positions the n1-standard-2 in the lower performance brackets across compute and memory workloads. The single-core stress-ng metric reached 1103.99, while multi-core performance measured 1451.07. Similarly, Geekbench registered scores of 936.0 for single-core and 1106.0 for multi-core processing, ranking in the bottom 10 percent of evaluated systems. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth peaked at 13.5 GB/sec, with write bandwidth recording 11.46 GB/sec. Application tests recorded 1.39 million operations per second for Redis SET commands and 1.6 GB/sec for static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-2 represents an entry-tier configuration of an older generation hardware architecture. Because compute density and instruction throughput are modest compared to contemporary standards, the server trades absolute performance for accessible dedicated resource allocation. It is best suited for non-intensive workloads, including low-traffic web serving, development environments, microservices, light data preprocessing, and entry-level background tasks.

Configured with 8.0 GB of memory, the system provides a balanced general-purpose allocation of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. Benchmark metrics place the server in the lower baseline tiers, reflecting its legacy x86_64 processor profile with Geekbench scores of 936.0 single-core and 1106.0 multi-core, and large-block memory read bandwidth of 13.5 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput measures 1.39 million operations per second, with static web serving reaching 1.6 GB/sec. Due to its modest computational capacity, the instance is appropriate for utility services, testing pipelines, and lightweight web hosting.
